newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator blasts Swiss Holocaust victims plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator blasts Swiss Holocaust victims plan.

text.p: - U.S. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato on Wednesday blasted a Swiss government decision to set up and administer a memorial fund to aid Holocaust victims, saying the Swiss had failed in the past to administer such a fund properly.

In a statement, D'Amato said: "The money doesn't belong to them. The money was looted from Holocaust victims and should be returned to them. The Swiss must find whose money was looted, how much there is and return it -- all of it."

D'Amato's unexpected response came just hours after Edgar Bronfman, president of the World Jewish Congress, and other Jewish leaders hailed the Swiss government announcement as historic and creating a new chapter in Swiss-Jewish relations.
The senator, WJC leaders, Swiss and U.S. government officials are scheduled to meet Friday in New York to discuss details of the fund, including how it is to be managed and who would be aided.

Switzerland said on Wednesday it would create a fund tapping more than $70 million in contributions from banks and other businesses to aid Holocaust victims and consider making contributions to the fund itself later in the year.

But D'Amato said Swiss efforts to manage a 1962 fund to distribute unclaimed jewish assets failed with the Swiss not adequately notifying claimants. "I am concerned that the Swiss government is trying to follow the same pattern today. We cannot do business as usual," the senator said.
